evidence: Several probes: build_corpus('tiny', root, fixture_fetch) and then build_corpus('full', same root, reduced targets or stubbed assembly) gave 'tiny trained True vocab 4096', 'full trained False', the same tokenizer hash (3c06b03e6f9b) or a byte-identical tokenizer.json, and manifest scale 'full' for all 8 datasets with no tokenizer provenance key. Held-out bytes/token: 2.070 (tiny --fixtures tokenizer), 3.081 (1.5 MB sample), 3.109 (13 MB sample). test_build.py:836-845 confirms shared artifacts are reused in partial builds. corpus_dir() and tokenizer_path() are scale-independent.
fix: Record the tokenizer's and shared artifacts' provenance when they are made: a sidecar (e.g. tokenizer/tok-v1/build.json) or manifest field with scale, sample bytes, seed and corpus version. At --scale full, raise BuildError (exit 1, plain message to add --retrain-tokenizer or use another --out) when the existing tokenizer or simple_vocab/known_vocab/false_facts were made at another scale or have no record; or retrain automatically when all datasets are being built. Apply the VOCAB_SIZE check to a reused tokenizer too. Make tiny builds default to a separate root (e.g. data/tiny) or refuse to overwrite a full corpus. Drop 'tiny' from cli.py BUILD_DATA_HINT or say it needs its own --out. Update CLAUDE.md accordingly and add a 'tiny then full' test.

scenario: Before the hours-long `--scale full` run, the owner or the local Task 15 session runs `airace-content build --scale tiny` (from the Hub or with --fixtures) into the default data root as a quick check. CLAUDE.md lists both scales with the same default output, and the airace-ml missing-tokenizer hint says 'airace-content build --scale tiny (a quick test set) or --scale full'. That build trains data/tokenizer/tok-v1/tokenizer.json on about 1,200 small documents (or about 40 KB of fixtures). The later `--scale full` finds the file, sets train_tok to False, loads the tiny tokenizer as frozen and encodes all ~137M tokens with it. The vocab-size check runs only for a freshly trained tokenizer, and a tiny tokenizer reaches 4096 entries anyway. Nothing records the scale the tokenizer was trained at: the manifest marks every dataset 'full', and the only sign is the summary line 'tokenizer: frozen, reused'. tok-v1 is frozen permanently, so the novelty index, the judge, the gate and every future player model inherit it. The measured cost of the --fixtures tiny tokenizer is about 50% more tokens for the same English (2.07 vs 3.08-3.11 bytes/token held out). A partial `--scale full --datasets X` build into a tiny-built root (which Task 15 step 3 prescribes) also reuses the tiny simple_vocab.txt and known_vocab.txt, so real web quality is scored against a few hundred known words and Standard/Thorough cleaning drops most of web. The reverse is also unguarded: a later tiny build into the same root overwrites the full corpora and shared artifacts.
title: A full corpus build silently reuses (and freezes as tok-v1) a tokenizer and shared vocab files left by an earlier tiny build in the same data root; the airace-ml CLI itself suggests the tiny build

evidence: Read the locked library sources (datasets file_utils.py:53-67, 830-871, 966-1002; parquet.py:84-234; load.py:1093-1182; huggingface_hub _http.py:451-559, _pagination.py:27-48, hf_file_system.py:1178-1250). Probe late_fail.py: a tiny build through cli.main with a fetch raising ConnectionError('Server Disconnected') in the last source (cosmo_stories) escaped as a traceback through build.py:346 and nothing was written under --out. Probe resume_wrapper.py: a Fetch-level retry wrapper that skips already-yielded rows, against a fetch failing every 97th row, produced a corpus byte-identical to an uninterrupted build, while a naive restart from row 0 changed it.
fix: Add a retry and exact-resume loop inside hf_fetch (about 40 lines plus offline tests with a fake `datasets` module): retry load_dataset as well as iteration; keep ds.state_dict() after each row and on a transient error sleep (30 s, 60, 120, ...), load_state_dict and continue, preserving 'same seed, same corpus'. Treat ConnectionError, TimeoutError, httpx.TransportError and HfHubHTTPError with status None or in {408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504} as transient; never retry DatasetNotFoundError, 401/403/404, SourceFormatError or BaseException; cap at about 8 attempts over about 30 min and print one flushed stderr line per retry. In cli.py catch the final transient error with a plain 'network problem, run the same command again' line. Before assembling, open every source the selected recipes use (plus tinystories), read a few rows and run row_has_format, failing fast. Tell the owner to run `python -m uv run --extra content hf auth login` (or set HF_TOKEN) first. Later, optionally stage each assembled dataset on disk keyed by scale/seed/recipe so a rerun skips finished sources.
scenario: hf_fetch is a generator, so each source is first contacted only when its dataset's turn comes; a full build makes 14 opens over the hour (tinystories for simple_vocab, then fineweb, gutenberg, cosmo_khan/wikihow/openstax, fineweb_edu, soda, everyday_conv, mbpp, gsm8k, simplewiki, tinystories, cosmo_stories). Every assembled document stays in memory until the writes at build.py:385-417, and cli.py:144 catches only BuildError, SourceFormatError and DatasetsUnavailable. With the locked libraries (datasets 5.1.0, huggingface_hub 1.33.0, fsspec 2026.7.0): reads survive network loss of up to about 9-10 minutes and 429s (byte-exact retries), but the tree listing, repo_info and dataset_info calls at each open have no retry, so a single 429/5xx/connection error there aborts; and during reads, datasets retries only 504 and 429, so a burst of 500/502/503 over about 25 s aborts. A config change, a hub error or a format problem in a late source (e.g. after the Task 15 simplewiki license decision; FORMAT_CHECK_ROWS only runs once the source is reached) also aborts. Each occurrence loses the whole hour (failure at the creative sources loses nearly all of it), shows the owner a raw traceback for hub errors, writes nothing, and the rerun streams everything again. Estimated about 1-5% per run on a stable wired connection, more on Wi-Fi or a shared IP.
title: The hour-long full build has no retry, resume or source pre-flight: a Hub error when any of the 14 sources is opened, a 500/502/503 lasting over ~25 s, or a late format/config error discards all streamed work with a traceback
